newsitem.title: CHINA: China current debt level reasonable - paper.
newsitem.headline: China current debt level reasonable - paper.

text.p: China's foreign debt level is reasonable and there are no plans for a sharp reduction in debt growth, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Beijing should strengthen examination of borrowing applications but there was no reason not to use foreign credits to finance key projects, the newspaper quoted an official of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange Control as saying.
"The present growth of external debt is reasonable in view of the country's payment ability and economic demand," the Business Weekly quoted the official as saying.
"The annual payment of principal and interest, which is about $10 billion a year, is well within the country's capacity regarding foreign currency reserves," she said.
As of June, the country's total outstanding foreign debt was $109.57 billion, the newspaper said, quoting official statistics.
Foreign exchange reserves reached $95 billion at the end of September and were expected to top $100 billion by the end of the year, according to central bank officials.
"It's unwise for us not to take advantage of the abundant funds in the international money market, for which other Asian nations are vying fiercely," the official said.
China's debt sevice ratio was 7.3 percent last year, well within the recognised safety level of 20 percent, according to the newspaper.

The newspaper said the nation's debt composition had also improved as mid- and long-term debt accounted for $98 billion, or 89.4 percent of total debt, as of June compared with 88.8 percent last year. Short-term debt was about $11.6 billion.
